Static publish executes #+BEGIN_QUERY blocks (title + bounded results) through the same public-only capability as {{query}}; rows filtered as non-public are reported as a count only, and malformed payloads fail closed (no raw payload in HTML or the search index)
entries.notes: Martin-approved Q2 delta (2026-07-21 sweep). Publish already ran {{query}} via render_query with publish_page_allowed filtering; BEGIN_QUERY containers were inert source. Now: whole-container detection mirrors the frontend BeginQuery.tsx contract (delimiters, balanced EDN, :title string, :query vector); the query source is sliced from raw and delegated to the existing bounded/cached render_query; the publication snapshot includes ALL freshly parsed pages so omitted private matches can be counted honestly, while HTML hydration capability remains public-only; a muted query-omitted note reports the count (all-pages-public never shows it); malformed containers render an inert alert and their payload is excluded from the search index; print keeps its whole-graph behavior. Fail-before (worker-run, Sol/high): 2 publish_begin_query tests fail pre-fix. Full publish suite 34 pass + whole tine-core 514 pass (manager-run).

Bounded query and reference results cap occurrence construction and retain every warm result family across unrelated edits, including pages with unchanged aliases, without preserving stale overflow metadata
Android 9 / API 28 launches Tine without an unresolved renameat2 symbol in libtine_lib.so
entries.notes: Reopened 2026-07-22 after the reporter reproduced the same loader crash on v0.6.2. Direct inspection of the published v0.6.4 arm64 APK proved libtine_lib.so still imported undefined renameat2: the first fix covered backup.rs but missed the Android-built model.rs trash path. The second call now uses the syscall entry point, and an actual packaged debug APK (SHA-256 d2c8280524ca9adaf450d62f44efb735ada1d381eff55625e5c47cf137e2561f) imports syscall but not renameat2. The release workflow now enforces the same symbol-table gate on the canonical APK. Android 9 device confirmation remains desirable but is no longer the only protection against recurrence.

entries.notes: GH #246 accepted harm: an eligible non-empty document outside pages/ could appear blank, external add/delete stayed invisible, and editing the blank state could overwrite real bytes. The base reproduction at be54af62 failed because list_pages/find_entry/load_by_path only admitted configured pages/journals roots. This row also covers OG-compatible lowercase .markdown through bootstrap/source capture, exact projection, external reconciliation/feed, edit/writeback/delete observation, configured-root rename spelling preservation, and .md/.markdown/.org same-stem twin refusal.

entries.notes: P3.1 contract tests cover LocalActive to SharePrepared to SharedActive for the initiator, LocalActive to Joining to SharedActive for a peer, duplicate/reordered descriptor delivery, malformed partial bootstrap evidence, split-genesis descriptor conflict, dirty unique local tail, portable projection/base mismatch, and every named enrollment record/head crash cut. entries.title: Sparse-oplog editor saves use actor-owned identity and ordering and refuse stale or ambiguous page state without a second writer
entries.notes: Covers OG-normalized name-and-kind lookup across nested .md/.markdown/.org paths, duplicate-owner ambiguity, actor-issued revisions, whole-outline edit/insert/move/reorder/delete, configured page and journal creation, pre-enqueue bounds and cycle checks, stale external-edit refusal, and retained-publication retry through the sole operational coordinator.

entries.title: Explicit sparse-v2 app activation drains legacy authority, routes whole-root watcher input through one actor, and refuses unproven clean shutdown
entries.notes: The app persists stable caller-owned activation identities only after every tracked legacy Graph lease drains, while graph refresh and migration share the same transition lock, then publishes exactly one sparse actor or a visible retryable/blocked binding. The recursive root watcher closes its installation interval with one full reconciliation, keeps nested and case-variant Markdown/Org events incremental, and ignores explicit unmanaged file events. The journey activates a pre-populated nested Unicode graph without rewriting its bytes, confirms exact bootstrap receipts, authors and queries through the exact adjacent-tagged actor wire, imports an external edit through the watcher queue, reaches Safe shutdown, exposes stopped runtime as retryable, reopens authenticated LocalActive state, and proves legacy routes remain refused. Focused core cuts prove one-time receipt confirmation resumes before actor publication and a later missing private completion blocks reconciliation without changing externally edited graph bytes.

entries.title: Two sparse-v2 devices explicitly share one descriptor-bound lineage and converge bounded filesystem-provider delivery without authorizing partial or conflicting evidence
entries.notes: Covers commit-last prepare-share and crash-resume from SharePrepared, incremental clean join beyond 4,096 provider entries and 8 MiB, both SharedActive roles across restart, reopening more than 64 settled manifests without historical replay, crash-resumable dependency-closed publication including unsafe local-manifest repair after private pending-marker creation failure, independent poll-mode provider delivery, coalesced incomplete-manifest rechecks after adversely reordered exact object delivery, nested nonstandard Unicode Markdown/Org paths, reordered and duplicate delivery, partial bootstrap and split-genesis refusal, dirty unique local-tail refusal, partition/rejoin, receiver-local projection, superseded-frontier rollback refusal, and convergence. A canonical generated Syncthing or Dropbox conflict copy is removed only after exact path, canonical-content, byte-equality, and no-follow retirement proof; differing, absent-target, malformed, or ambiguous evidence remains byte-exact and visibly blocks without graph writes. Continuously unstable full-scan epochs retain their fence and yield to retry backoff after one retry rebase. Tauri exposes bounded explicit prepare/join actions only inside the experimental sparse-v2 Settings flow, keeps provider polling separate from graph-wide reconciliation, and replaces stopped handles with retryable reopen slots after a transient post-transition reopen failure.

entries.title: Reverse-delivered provider histories use dependency-indexed readiness work while retaining every blocked batch
entries.notes: The fail-before/pass-after stress receipt used a 96-batch linear history delivered newest-first: the indexed scheduler converged with exactly 96 manifest registrations while the prior pending-deque scan performed 9,216 readiness inspections. The always-on 24-batch regression preserves the same quadratic discriminator without adding a four-minute suite cost. A focused index neighbor covers multiple parents, an already-active synthetic base head, duplicate registration, unrelated acceptance, exact edge work, and deterministic sibling wake order. Existing shared-provider journeys continue to cover duplicate exact delivery, incomplete manifests becoming complete, restart reconstruction, publication repair, status visibility, and Safe-shutdown refusal while inbound evidence remains blocked.

entries.title: SharedActive startup discovers immutable device frontiers without replaying settled provider history
entries.notes: A genuine Safe reopen over more than 64 settled manifests enumerates one device head, authenticates only the exact manifests selected by that bounded head payload, and reads zero provider objects or broad historical manifest paths. Unseen device tips walk exact immutable manifests and digest-addressed objects through the dependency index; empty prototype namespaces fall back once and migrate automatically. Complete namespace repair withholds every head and Safe until bounded recovery-mirror backfill plus canonical manifest/object closure repair settle, while retiring each exact manifest-bound crash-ordering intent after that batch's durable repair. The permanent regression uses an isolated test-only head-scan cap of 8 over 12 accepted historical batches and a mirror-before-canonical crash cut; the production cap remains 4,096. Crash cuts before head publication and before old-head retirement, unsafe reopen, duplicate/reordered device heads, generated conflict copies, malformed evidence, and deleted own heads remain bounded and cannot let Safe outrun durable discovery publication. Superseded-head retirement also converges when provider deletion wins before the first local remove, and a later redelivery is retired through the ordinary journal path, including after completed-retirement provider evidence disappears.

entries.title: Recovery-covered provider heads preserve missing canonical ancestor availability for stale peers
entries.notes: Every ordinary manifest publication durably writes an exact batch link and immutable digest-addressed recovery copy before canonical manifest visibility. Recovery authority is bound to the exact accepted-frontier acceptance sequence and state digest: each newly accepted local or provider batch invalidates the prior authority and enters a bounded exact mirror queue, while uncovered legacy state uses bounded cursor backfill. Only a durable current-root covered head can initialize authority on reopen, and no covered head or Safe can outrun mirror, canonical manifest, required object, or dependency-closure repair. Normal intact reopen authenticates only bounded head-selected tips and reads no recovery copies or historical namespace. Permanent same-document regressions cover a missing middle canonical ancestor and the stronger reordered case where a previously covered receiver accepts canonical/object bytes without the mirror, authors a child, crashes, and cannot publish a covered child head or reach Safe before local mirror backfill. After restart and queue settlement, deleting only the middle canonical still lets a stale third peer reconstruct and converge from duplicate/reordered child, head, link, and blob delivery without either author returning. Crash cuts before recovery and after recovery but before canonical, generated conflicts, corruption, and deletion of both exact copies block visibly.

entries.title: Provider-visible immutable publication intents recover a complete manifest stranded before its covering frontier head
entries.notes: The permanent crash cut publishes immutable objects, canonical descriptor-bound intents, and matching manifests, then stops before a covering frontier head or watcher callback. A normal-startup receiver with an older valid head uses an isolated cap of 4 to discover 6 foreign intents across explicit cursor-preserving chunks. The regression proves the first boundary is neither EOF nor Safe and cannot publish a head, every intent and batch converges without a broad manifest/object scan, and only an actual EOF plus a covering receiver head permits complete foreign-intent retirement and genuine Safe. A two-device deletion-replication regression additionally proves that when a peer retires the author's intent first, the author's later covered retirement settles without a local journal record, accepts a subsequent peer page, and reaches Safe instead of starving inbound work. Missing or mismatched manifests and uncovered intents remain retryable, and the production per-chunk cap remains 4,096.

entries.title: Clean shutdown cannot publish an own head ahead of paused imprecise frontier discovery
entries.notes: A deterministic post-publication crash cut pauses an imprecise head cursor after descriptor discovery, installs a previously unseen foreign recovery-covered head and its complete batch, then recovers a concurrent local publication before requesting shutdown. The durable own head at the cut must already cover both local and foreign tips and current manifest recovery; descriptor/head/intent discovery remains bounded and does not enter manifest/object full-scan history. After the cut, own intent retirement settles and genuine Safe remains bounded. The provider-head oracle rejects tips without current manifest recovery coverage.

entries.title: Incomplete foreign delivery neither strands local publication nor gets outrun after its objects arrive
entries.notes: Realistic two-device helpers deliver manifests independently from immutable objects. The complete-delivery control converges and reaches Safe. In the frontier-decoupling attack arm, one device retains the foreign manifest as visible inbound work while publishing four unrelated local pages: every accepted local frontier gets a durable recovery-covered device head and its covered publication intent retires instead of accumulating. Safe remains refused while foreign objects are absent; restart restores the pending manifest, and late exact object delivery converges it. A second deterministic arm gives foreign and local no-op batches the identical content-addressed object set. The foreign manifest is staged first without that object; local admission then writes the shared object without a provider callback. A post-head crash cut proves the foreign batch is admitted and recovery-covered before the own head becomes durable. At exact base 6ae78827, the first arm failed with no advanced own head and intent counts [1, 2, 3, 4]; against the rejected frontier-decoupling patch before the arrival fix, the second arm failed because the own head omitted the now-Ready foreign batch.

entries.title: Two offline authors union concurrent frontier heads without either branch returning through the other endpoint first
entries.notes: The permanent regression authors two page batches offline from the same synthetic accepted base, unions both immutable device heads, and requires both endpoints to accept and project both branches without returning either author first. Provider dependency registration and blocked rechecks use authenticated accepted-frontier containment, including manifest-less synthetic and transitive accepted ancestors; page-specific projection authority preserves the exact stale-write fence across unrelated concurrent catalog heads.

entries.title: Historical projection frontiers cannot authorize a later portable-path reacquisition
entries.notes: The permanent local regression creates a Markdown page and renames it A→B→A→B, proving every round reaches durable projection instead of retrying against the original A frontier. Historical projection reuse is bound to the current portable-path owner and acquisition batch, and any existing local completion must uniquely match that lifecycle and target. The neighboring unrelated-frontier external-delete regression remains covered so the correction does not weaken intentional delete authority.

entries.title: Accepted headless no-op dependencies remain authenticated scheduler members after restart
entries.notes: The engine proof retains an accepted bootstrap no-op that has no document head and bounds membership to authenticated point reads over exact accepted status, append-only accepted sequence, accepted-batch map, and current accepted authority. The provider regression accepts a synthetic headless dependency, removes its provider manifest, restarts the receiver, duplicates and reorders a real CRDT child's delivery, and requires the child to settle without an absent-manifest shortcut.

entries.title: Config filename-policy changes cannot rename an exactly owned oplog page or journal on a later external edit
entries.notes: The page and journal regressions change config.edn, reopen from archived authority, apply the external reconciliation transaction, reopen a second time, and assert PageId, accepted logical name, semantic kind, textual referrers, and new-path policy. Every authenticated current-path row is point-checked against exact materialized catalog PageId state before join or import consumption; wrong name digest or kind fails before execution material exists, including after retained-run adoption. Scratch schema 12 and authenticated current-path catalog schema 1 transition to 13 and 2; a schema-12 retained run named by a valid resume point is preserved, refused, and rebuilt only by full immutable-history replay. A real old-path to new-path move still adopts the destination decode, and explicit Tine rename remains the graph-wide RenamePagesAndRewriteReferrers operation.
